title: Editor FOV sometimes changes after zooming out in orthogonal mode
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.5.1, 4.4.1 This might be a regression, because I don't recall having this issue in earlier versions, but maybe I just didn't zoom out far enough. Tested 4.5.1 and 4.4.1 so far. ### System information Godot v4.5.1.stable - Ubuntu 25.10 25.10 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU - AMD Ryzen 5 5600H with Radeon Graphics (12 threads) - 13.50 GiB memory ### Issue description When I switch my in-editor view of a 3D scene to "Top" (with orthogonal projection) and then press "Switch perspective/orthogonal view" to get back, sometimes the FOV becomes really warped. I think this is related to zoom level. If I then go to "View - Settings", the editor claims that the FOV is still the standard 70; when I press "OK" in that window, FOV fixes itself. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new 3D scene or use an existing one. The renderer doesn't matter, I've been able to reproduce it with both Forward+ and Compatibility. You may add a capsule if you like for better visual feedback, but the axis arrows should be an obvious enough indicator of the bug. 2. Press Kp7 or choose "Top" in the "Perspective" menu. 3. **Crucial step:** Zoom out with Ctrl / - a few times. I'm still not sure where the threshold is; I might've been able to reproduce this with as little as 7 presses, but it might depend on the distance from the origin, so try 20-ish just to be sure. The amount of warp also seems dependent on the distance. 4. Press Kp5 or choose "Switch Perspective/Orthogonal view" in the "Perspective" menu. Now you should see the increased FOV as depicted below. If you're unable to reproduce the bug, try steps 2-3 again but zoom out even further. 5. If you now press "View - Settings", you'll see that the system thinks that this is FOV 70. Clearly it's not. 6. Press OK and everything is indeed back to the normal 70. I think this doesn't require an MRP? ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
